name: Approval Chance Predictor
description: Get a realistic percentage chance of approval before you submit a verification application, based on the same details reviewers use to reject applications. Built for businesses applying for verification and for agencies managing many client applications at once.

notes.what: Starts your workflow when someone fills out and submits a web form you built
notes.overview: Build a public CtrlChecks form and start the workflow when someone submits structured answers, files, or intake details.
tips: Use friendly labels for submitters and stable internal names for workflow mapping.
Map answers with {{$json.customer_email}} or {{$json.data.customer_email}} after checking a test execution.
Use select or radio options for values that drive routing, approvals, reporting, or branch conditions.
Turn CAPTCHA on for public forms that can create tickets, leads, or notifications.
Require authentication only for internal or sensitive forms.
Changing an internal name after downstream nodes are mapped requires updating those mappings too.
notes.why: Collects the exact details a verification reviewer checks, so the prediction is based on the same inputs a real reviewer would see.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Pulls this client's existing readiness record so the prediction builds on the earlier Readiness Checker result instead of starting from nothing. Filtered to one client — without the filter the AI would receive every client in your table.

config.prompt: Compare this business against the most common reasons Meta/Google verification applications get rejected (mismatched business details, missing privacy policy, unverifiable address, inconsistent documents). Business: {{input.businessName}}, address {{input.address}}, website {{input.website}}. Existing readiness data: {{input.records}}. List every risk factor found, one per line starting with "RISK:".

notes.what: Sends your prompt to OpenAI's ChatGPT and gets back an AI-written response
notes.overview: Calls OpenAI through the legacy LLM adapter. Prompt is the main input; Messages is only a fallback when Prompt is blank. Temperature and Memory are visible legacy fields ignored by the current executor.
notes.why: Compares the business against the reasons applications actually get rejected. It outputs one 'RISK:' line per problem found, which the next step counts.

notes.what: Writes and runs any JavaScript you like to transform or process your data
notes.overview: Run sandboxed JavaScript once against the current workflow data and return the transformed value for downstream nodes.
tips: Always return the value the next node should receive
Default timeout is 5000ms and runtime caps at 30000ms
Use Output Schema such as {"type":"object"} only as a top-level shape hint
JavaScript has no credentials; connect downstream service node accounts separately
Do not paste API keys, tokens, or passwords into code
notes.why: Turns the AI's risk lines into a single number a client understands. Each risk costs 12 points off a 95% base — change those numbers here to make the estimate stricter or softer.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Writes the score back onto the same client row so the prediction is on file next time anyone opens the record.

config.message:
:bar_chart: Approval prediction for *{{input.businessName}}*: {{input.approvalPercentage}}% likely to pass.
Risks: {{input.risks}}

notes.what: Sends messages using a Slack app or bot connection
notes.overview: Send Slack bot messages to channels, direct messages, or existing threads through a saved Slack OAuth2 connection. Use it for workplace alerts, support replies, incident updates, approvals, report summaries, and deployment notifications.
tips: Select a Slack OAuth2 connection; do not paste bot tokens into message fields
The Slack app needs chat:write, and the bot must be invited before it can post in private channels
Use {{$json.channelId}} and {{$json.threadTs}} from Slack Trigger to reply in the same conversation
Keep Message filled as readable fallback text even when Blocks contains a rich Block Kit layout
Connect downstream service accounts separately; Slack OAuth2 only authorizes the Slack send
notes.why: Gives your verification team a heads-up on weak applications before the client chases them.

config.body:
Hi {{input.businessName}},

Based on your current details, we estimate a {{input.approvalPercentage}}% chance of passing verification on your next attempt.

We will follow up with next steps shortly.
config.subject: Your estimated approval chance: {{input.approvalPercentage}}%

notes.what: Send emails from your Gmail account or read and search messages in your inbox
notes.overview: Send, list, get, or search Gmail messages. Send recipients can be typed manually or extracted from upstream/fallback Google Sheets rows.
tips: Connect Google OAuth in Connections; do not paste tokens into workflow fields
Gmail search syntax: from:, subject:, is:unread, has:attachment
List/Search only return {id, threadId} per message â€” use a Get step with that id for full content
Body is plain text only
Get returns Gmail's raw API message; the body text is base64url-encoded inside message.payload.body.data
Use search to filter messages before getting details
notes.why: Sends the client their number. This is the deliverable — everything above exists to make this email accurate.
